To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed genetically targetable voltage-sensitive dyes by attaching a synthetic fluorescent dye to a SpyTag, a small peptide that binds and forms a covalent link with SpyCatcher.
we have developed a genetically encoded cell-surface receptor that enables covalent attachment of chemically synthesized voltage indicators to living cells.
we synthesized a new family of fluorescein-based, voltage-sensitive dyes with carboxylic acids for covalent conjugation to SpyTag, a small peptide that binds to its binding partner SpyCatcher.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of genetically targetable voltage indicators for imaging voltage dynamics in living neurons.
the development of new methods for optical measurement of membrane potential in living cells, and in particular the use of genetically targeted voltage indicators.
the development and application of novel genetically encoded voltage indicators for monitoring membrane potential in neurons and other cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the authors have successfully developed a new family of genetically targeted voltage-sensitive fluorescent dYES that can be used to image voltage changes in neurons with single cell and subcellular resolution.
the authors have developed a novel method to target voltage indicators to specific cell populations.

this study presents a new family of genetically targeted voltage-sensitive fluorescent dyls that can be co-valently attached to genetically encoded receptors to achieve voltage imaging in genetically defined neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we developed a novel method that combines genetically encoded voltage sensors and chemical voltage indicators, and that this method enables fast, sensitive and genetically targeted voltage imaging in living cells.
genetically targeted synthetic indicators can be developed for fast optical measurement of neuronal membrane potential with high spatial resolution.
we developed a new family of voltage-sensitive fluorescent dves (VoltageFluor) and genetically targeted them to the cell surface using the SpyTag/SpyCatcher system.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the combination of chemical synthesis and genetic targeting enables a new class of voltage probes with the potential to provide high-resolution, high-speed voltage imaging from genetically targeted cells.
genetically targeted synthetic voltage indicators are a promising tool for optical measurement of action potential dynamics in genetically defined cells.
genetically targeted chemical voltage indicators offer an attractive alternative to genetically encoded indicators for voltage imaging in living cells.
